lines.say: Ten rockets, so ten back? That's what most people think proportionate means.
The laws of war say something else.
Is the expected harm to civilians excessive, compared with the concrete military advantage?
It is never a body count contest between two sides.
Now, city battles fought by other armies.
Mosul, 2016 to 2017. Nine to eleven thousand civilians killed.
Raqqa, 2017. Over 1,600 civilians killed by coalition strikes.
And Gaza? How many of the dead were civilians is disputed.
Israeli officials said about half. Leaked IDF data, reported in the press, suggested 83 percent. The IDF disputes it.
Gaza's civilian toll is real and heavy. Every strike can be judged, by the law, with one yardstick for everyone.
Per strike, or by body count? How would you judge it? Tell me below.
If you love Israeli facts, follow Noam Roz for more.
Not ten for ten. One strike at a time.

caption_en:
Proportionate doesn't mean what most people think. ⚖️

Under the laws of war, proportionality is a test for each single strike: is the expected harm to civilians excessive compared with the concrete and direct military advantage? (Additional Protocol I, 1977, Art. 51(5)(b) and 57; ICRC Customary IHL, Rule 14). It is never a comparison of death tolls between two sides.

City battles fought by other armies: Dresden 1945, up to 25,000 people killed (Dresden Historians' Commission, 2010). Mosul 2016 to 2017, 9,000 to 11,000 civilians (AP, Dec 2017). Raqqa 2017, more than 1,600 civilians killed by coalition strikes (Amnesty International and Airwars, 2019).

Gaza: the Gaza Ministry of Health (HAMAS run) counted about 67,000 dead by Oct 2025, without a civilian split. The civilian share is disputed: Israeli officials said about half (May 2024); leaked IDF data reported by the Guardian, +972 and Local Call suggested 83% (Aug 2025); the IDF disputes it.

Gaza's civilian toll is real and heavy. Every strike can be judged: by the law, with one yardstick for everyone.

Per strike, or by body count: how would you judge it?

Sources: Additional Protocol I (1977); ICRC Customary IHL Rule 14; Dresden Historians' Commission (2010); AP (2017); Amnesty International and Airwars (2019); Netanyahu (May 2024); Guardian, +972, Local Call (Aug 2025).

caption_he:
מידתיות זה לא "ירו 10 טילים, יורים 10 בחזרה".
לפי דיני המלחמה בודקים כל תקיפה בנפרד: האם הנזק הצפוי לאזרחים מופרז ביחס ליתרון הצבאי. זו אף פעם לא השוואה של מספרי הרוגים.
קרבות ערים של צבאות אחרים: דרזדן 1945, עד 25,000 הרוגים. מוסול 2016 עד 2017, 9,000 עד 11,000 אזרחים. רקה 2017, יותר מ-1,600 אזרחים.
בעזה, שיעור האזרחים מבין ההרוגים שנוי במחלוקת. המחיר האזרחי אמיתי וכבד, ושופטים כל תקיפה לפי החוק, באותו סרגל לכולם.
לפי תקיפה או לפי מספר הרוגים: איך אתם הייתם שופטים?
